description:
FILED s407 (fable-answers-s406.md §4.7, from s405 §1.5).  `timeout` killed the
SBCL it started; the spinning GRANDCHILD (spawned by tools/pclperl-for-tests
inside it) was orphaned and burned one of sixteen cores at 99.9% for 3516 s
through every measurement of that session — and nothing in the runner noticed.
Same family as #273 (orphaned pl2cl --server; its own reaper is now the
getppid tick).
SHAPE: run each test file in its OWN process group / session (setsid, or
POSIX::setpgid in the forked worker before exec) in tools/run-perl-suite.pl and
sweep-perl-tests.pl, and on TIMEOUT kill(-$pgid, TERM) then KILL after a grace
period; report "killed N descendants" in the row.  Keep the direct-child kill as
the belt.  Also worth a `--census` line at the end of a run: any surviving
process whose cmdline names the run's temp dir.
BAR (runners row): the runner that changed, once, verdicts compared file-by-file
before/after; a deliberate spin fixture (a .t whose PCL child loops) proves the
group dies; PCL_SHOW_SBCL=1 unchanged.


DONE s408 (Opus 5).  THE PREMISE NEEDED SHARPENING, and that is the finding:
`timeout` ALREADY kills the process GROUP it created -- measured, a plain
grandchild dies with it.  What escapes is anything SBCL starts: sb-ext:run-program
puts its child in a NEW PROCESS GROUP (measured: the child's PID == its PGID),
so the group signal cannot reach it.  setpgrp does NOT change the SESSION, so
the session is the handle that still does.

SHIPPED: each file's command runs in its own session (fork + POSIX::setsid,
`timeout` unchanged INSIDE it) and whatever is left in that session afterwards
is TERMed then KILLed; count reported per row.  Both runners.

PROVEN by a deliberate spin fixture (a .t whose PCL child spins): it survives a
plain timeout (PID left behind, measured) and is reaped by the runner.  NOT
hypothetical -- a full companion run reaped orphans from FOUR real files, EIGHT
of them from op/alarm.t alone.

MISTAKE WORTH KEEPING: the orphan count first went into $sig BEFORE the status
was computed, which turned op/alarm.t (5/0 vs perl 5/0) into a DIFF.  Reaping an
orphan is an observation about the RUN, never a divergence.

BAR: PCL_SHOW_SBCL byte-identical for both runners; companion verdicts compared
file-by-file (4 differ: the $sig bug above, 2 row re-blessings, op/cond.t's
SIGTERM); SWEEP verdicts compared file-by-file over 108 files: ZERO differ,
GATE clean.
subject: A hung PCL child OUTLIVES the run: both runners must kill the process GROUP on TIMEOUT (setsid + kill(-pgid)), not just the direct child
